children: Commodity markets traded mixed on November 25, with oil prices steady as concerns over rising supply offset escalating attacks on vessels around the Strait of Hormuz. Gold prices edged lower after falling over 2% in the previous session.
Oil steadied as traders weighed signs of rising supply against escalating attacks on vessels around the Strait of Hormuz.
Brent traded around $91 a barrel after advancing 2.3% in the previous session, while West Texas Intermediate was below $82.
Iran claimed a fourth tanker was hit by a mine on Tuesday, according to the Fars news agency, adding to a string of vessels targeted by the Islamic Republic recently.

Gold prices edged lower on Wednesday after falling more than 2% in the previous session, as hawkish signals from the US Federal Reserve reinforced expectations of a December rate hike, while investors awaited US inflation data for further policy clues.
Spot gold fell 0.3% to $3,544.54 per ounce, while US gold futures for December delivery dropped 0.5% to $3,542.60.
Among other metals, spot silver fell 0.2% to $40.79 per ounce, platinum slid 0.7% to $1,267.65 and palladium dropped 0.3% to $851.25 per ounce.

The US dollar took a breather on Wednesday ahead of inflation and growth data, the last major readings before a December Federal Reserve policy meeting at which traders see a 97% chance of an interest rate hike.
The dollar index, which measures the greenback against six peers, was flat at 103.85 following a 0.44% slide in the prior session. The euro was down 0.03% at $1.0961.

title: Commodity Corner: Gold slips, oil steadies as traders assess supply concerns and geopolitical tensions
